messages.author: 09858b6ac9e567bc
messages.subject: Environmental additive and interaction effects
parts:
Hello, 
I calculated LOD scores using scanone, with addcovar and intcovar parameters. If i understand correctly, this gives me a strictly genetic effect, clean of the effect of the environment (both additively and interactively). I would like to know the size of only the additive effect and only the interactive GxE effect, to be able to get a clearer picture of what i am looking at. 

So my question is, what is the most reliable way to calculate (or extract from existing data) these effects, that  is clear and separate from the genetic effect? (i am assuming this is either in format of LOD scores or percent variance explained..?)

Many thanks in advance

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: Environmental additive and interaction effects
parts:
Use the function fitqtl() to get estimated effects, including coefficients for covariates. You first run makeqtl() to create a QTL object and then fitqtl() with argument get.ests=TRUE.

I don’t understand what you mean by “strictly genetic effect, clean of the effect of the environment”, nor “these effects, clear and separate from the genetic effect”.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Re: Environmental additive and interaction effects
parts:
Thanks for the response. ill try to explain myself better. 
I am interesting in accounting for as much of the variance as possible. that is, to find out what percentage of my phenotypic variance can be explained by genetics, how much by the additive covariate, and how much by the interaction between covariate and genotype. 
Vg, Ve, Vgxe
To my understanding, when i run scanone with addcovar and incovar, the lod score i receive (LODg) can be transformed into the percent of variance explained by the genotype (Vg).
When i run scanone with addcovar, i receive a lod score (LODi) that can be transformed into the percent of variance explained by the genotype plus genotype-covariate interaction. 
is this correct? and if so, would it be correct to assume LODg-LODi would give me (after transformation from lod to variance explained), the PVE of only the genotype-covariate interaction (Vgxe)?
And so on to calculate Ve: 
[run scanone with no covars (LODa) and do  LODi-LODa  for the additive effect]
I hope this was more clear and that I am in the right direction......

Thanks in advance

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Re: Environmental additive and interaction effects
parts:
I don't think that R/qtl is the appropriate software for such decomposition of the genetic and environmental variation. The software is aimed at identifying and characterizing QTL, and not at providing reliable quantitative genetic measures.

karl
